title: Sam Wants a Raise
text: Sam finds you at the end of a long shift with a printed sheet: what crew with Sam's rating get on the other ships on the board, and what Sam gets here. "I'm taking it up to the captain tomorrow," Sam says. "I'd like you there."

plays.text: You log it as a fall on the ladder. Sam takes the next three galley shifts without being asked, and has the dent knocked out of the panel by the end of the week.

title: Galley Brawl
text: Sam got drunk on something kept in a water bottle and put their head into the galley bulkhead. There's a dent in the panel, blood on the deck, and Sam on the floor with a cloth pressed to their forehead. The dressing and the stitches come out of the medical stores, about 3,000 cr of them, and the stores are logged.

plays.text: Sam takes the call in the hold, with the lag, a hand over their mouth for most of it. They come back with red eyes and don't say what was said. For the rest of the week they hum in the corridors.
plays.mem: 9 Jun 2214: You paid for my call home.

title: Homesick
text: Sam has been quiet for days, pushing food round the plate at meals. At night you've seen them at the viewport. They haven't said anything about Mars.

title: Bad Dreams
text: Sam hasn't been sleeping. There are shadows under their eyes, they drop small tools, and they jump at every clank of the hull. When you ask, they tell you in a flat voice. "The same one every night. There's a crack in the plating by my bunk, and it opens, and there's no sound."

plays.text: Sam sits down and gives you an hour of it: names, debts, who left whom at which port. In the middle of it is one thing you can use: "The governor's office on Juno Commons is buying Food for a reception, over the odds." Then Sam moves on to the next thing.

title: Gossip
text: Sam has been on the open band with half the ships in range. They know which freighter is behind on its lane fees, and who's walked off a crew at the next port. They lean in at your bunk with news.

plays.text: Sam looks at you. "Family business," Sam says. That's all you get. Afterwards Sam takes meals in the bunk and pulls the curtain to sleep.

title: Locked Locker
text: Sam's locker has two locks, the ship's and a cheap padlock over it. They've been getting messages with no sender ID, short ones, at odd hours. They read them, delete them, and read the next. When you come into the room, they put the slate face down.

plays.text: They find a hairline crack in an old fitting that has been weeping mass for months, and seal it with a strip of foil. You recover 25 units of reaction mass. The pumps run quieter after that.
plays.mem: 9 Jun 2214: You let me tinker.

plays.text: Something goes pop. A thin jet of reaction mass hisses out of the open housing before you can shut it, and you lose 20 units. Sam looks at the empty housing. "Ah," Sam says.

plays.text: They put every part back, muttering, and the pumps run as before. Sam tightens the last bolt without looking at you.

title: Tinkering
text: Sam has the reaction mass pumps in pieces on a sheet of plastic in the middle of the engine room, "to see how they go together". Every bolt is in a row. Three manuals are open, and there's a cup of cold tea. Nobody asked them to.

plays.text: You sit beside them in the dim light. For a few minutes nobody speaks. The drive hums. A pipe ticks. When it's done, you both sit a while. "Thank you," Sam says.
plays.mem: 9 Jun 2214: You prayed with me.

title: Quiet Prayer
text: Sam finds you in the galley at the turn of the watch with a worn charm in one hand, and asks you to join a short prayer for safe passage. They say it every burn, alone, in a corner, but tonight they wanted company. It takes a few minutes, and you can stay silent.

plays.text: You step between them. "Sit," you say. "Both of you." The room goes still. "Leave the humming alone," you say to Sam. Sam goes red, then pale, and leaves. For days Sam eats alone.
plays.mem: 9 Jun 2214: You took their side against me in front of everyone.

plays.text: You lean in the doorway with your arms folded and let them. It's short and loud, and the soup pot goes over. 8 points of hull damage later they're sitting side by side on the deck, sharing a cloth for a bloody lip. "It was flat," Sam says. "It was flat," says the other, and they both laugh.

title: Friction
text: Sam has been needling the rest of the crew for days: a jab at breakfast, a remark in the corridor, a dig at how someone hums. Tonight in the galley it's the humming again. A chair scrapes. "Say that again," says a level voice. "I said it was flat," Sam says. "I didn't say it was your fault. I said it was flat." "Say that again."

plays.text: You find Sam in the galley washing the last of the pots, and thank them. They wave it off and make a joke of it, and their ears go pink.

title: Small Kindnesses
text: Sam spent the night fixing everyone's bunk lights, one by one, with a screwdriver, and in the small hours cooked a real meal from the last of the good stores. Nobody asked them to. In the morning every bunk had a light that worked.

plays.text: You raise a cup, and so does everyone else, round the table. The bottle tastes of Mars: sweet, smoky, with something bitter under it. To the ship. To the crew. Somebody laughs, then everyone does, and the bottle goes round twice before it's empty.

title: Shared Bottle
text: Sam comes into the galley at the end of a long shift with a dusty bottle wrapped in a shirt. They've carried it in the bottom of their bag since they left Mars. They set it on the table and take down every cup in the cupboard. "I was keeping it for something," they say. "This'll do."

plays.text: Sam goes out through the lock with a tether and a bag of tools. For twenty minutes they're a bright shape against the stars, working along the hull. Then they're back inside, helmet off, sweating, holding the bent strut.

A tether snaps. For one second Sam drifts, arms out, until a gloved hand catches a handhold and holds. They make it back, shaking. The ship takes 13 points of damage from the loose mast, and nobody sleeps much that night.

You go out through the lock yourself, with the tether at your belt, and fix it in the cold and the silence with the ship turning slowly below your boots. It takes forty minutes. Sam watches through the port, and when you come in Sam hands you a cup and says nothing.
plays.mem: 9 Jun 2214: You took the risky EVA yourself.

title: Volunteer
text: A sensor mast has come loose in the burn and hangs by one strut, banging against the hull with every pulse of the drive. It'll tear free sooner or later and take plating with it. Before you can speak, Sam has the suit half on. "I'll go," they say, buckling a strap. "It's a ten-minute job."
